transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-06 15:30 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (Redwood CSM); Rajesh Patel (EdgeGate Infra Lead), Maya Flores (EdgeGate SRE), Ethan Cole (EdgeGate Security), Olivia Grant (EdgeGate Product)

Summary: quick sync on weekly POC results, new MTU-related packet loss seen on two on-prem racks, routing fallbacks, and runbook updates. Decided next canary tests and who owns kernel rollback drill.

--- Transcript ---
00:00 Ava Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining, we've got about 45 minutes, we'll run through the results, then MTU findings, then action items.
00:12 Rajesh Patel: thanks Ava, yeah quick note, we've been seeing these intermittent 100 to 200 ms spikes p95 on the staging cluster since last Friday, looks correlated with a bursty egress pattern to the VPC sidecar.
00:26 Liam Chen: okay got it, when you say sidecar is that the envoy egress proxy you have?
00:30 Rajesh Patel: yes envoy-ish, it's our egress proxy, sometimes it's labelled edge-proxy in the infra.
00:36 Maya Flores: and important, the packet drops seem to clean up after we tune MTU to 9000 but we haven't isolated if it's fragmentation or a path MTU discovery issue.
00:47 Liam Chen: hmmm path MTU discovery could be blocked by firewall ICMP rate-limit, that will cause PMTUD blackhole. we saw similar with a customer last quarter.
00:58 Ethan Cole: we do have ICMP rate limiting at the perimeter for DDoS protection, but can temporarily loosen for the canary window if required.
01:06 Ava Martinez: great, that matches what Redwood's telemetry hinted at: retransmits and small bursts during kernel preemption windows, which increase observed p95. we also noted increased kvcache misses on those requests.
01:20 Rajesh Patel: kv cache? are we talking Redwood's KV cache or internal memcached?
01:23 Liam Chen: Redwood KV cache — the platform keeps prefix KV in memory for tokens, if backend egress is slower the cache TTL hits and we fall back to full recompute which increases latency.
01:35 Olivia Grant: can you spell out the fallback behavior — so if the cache misses, do we route to another region or a model variant?
01:41 Priya Rao: good question, the POC is configured with regional fallback to the identical model on the next available pool and a lower-cost variant as a tertiary. routing policy is latency-first then cost.
01:52 Maya Flores: ok so a cache miss plus egress spike equals a cascade of longer tails.
01:57 Liam Chen: exactly. we observed p50 stays fine, p95 jumps. we recorded a 280 ms increase in one trace when the egress connection retried twice.
02:09 Rajesh Patel: we attached the trace in the sheet, there's a note about MTU mismatch between the on-prem switch and the VPC NAT.
02:16 Ava Martinez: thanks, we'll pull that up.
02:21 (short pause, typing)
02:30 Liam Chen: quick context on the runbook changes we propose: 1) MTU verification step during canary (iperf3 + traceroute -M), 2) temporary ICMP loosen for PMTUD for 30 minutes during test window, 3) kernel network offload toggles to try if fragmentation observed, 4) fallback rehearse script to validate model-variant routing.
02:55 Rajesh Patel: sounds good. for iperf we prefer rfc-compliant flags, and we will capture interface counters.
03:02 Maya Flores: note, our switch vendor has a known bug when jumbo frames cross a certain truncated VLAN—we'll include firmware id in the shared notes.
03:12 Ethan Cole: from a security perspective we need to log any temporary ICMP changes and have an approval email thread preserved. also KMS rotation windows might interfere with the test if they overlap.
03:24 Ava Martinez: understood, we'll include an approval template and also schedule tests outside of rotation windows.
03:30 Olivia Grant: can we talk about telemetry retention? the current pilot had only 7 days retention of raw token traces, not enough for our postmortems.
03:39 Priya Rao: we can extend telemetry retention for the pilot to 30 days as a trial; that will increase storage but gives you the full traces for root cause.
03:48 Rajesh Patel: ok please do that for staging and one canary region.
03:52 Liam Chen: moving to the numbers — p95 baseline from last week's run: 210 ms for small requests (<=128 tokens), during the surge event p95 jumped to 480 ms, error rate stayed low (~0.2%).
04:05 Maya Flores: do you have per-hop timings? the sheet shows a traceroute but the tool munged some hostnames so it's hard to interpret.
04:13 Liam Chen: yeah we noted the hostnames — sometimes traceroute hits a NAT and name flip happens, we'll scrub and annotate.
04:19 Rajesh Patel: timeline — we rolled kernel 5.10.93 on Apr 28 then observed the first spike on Apr 30 after a heavy egress pattern.
04:28 Ava Martinez: that is helpful. potential causes: kernel network buffering changes + MTU mismatch + ICMP filtered. the combined effect explains intermittent large tails.
04:40 Ethan Cole: what's the recommended rollback plan if the kernel upgrade is the root cause? we can't revert kernel in prod without windows.
04:46 Liam Chen: plan A is non-disruptive toggle: disable network offloads (GSO/GRO) on the instance to emulate pre-upgrade behavior, Plan B is targeted node drain and kernel rollback on specific racks as a controlled change with canary first.
04:59 Maya Flores: disabling offloads had a measurable CPU increase in prior tests — is that acceptable?
05:05 Liam Chen: small CPU bump, acceptable for short canary windows, we can monitor.
05:10 Rajesh Patel: who owns the runbook doc updates?
05:13 Ava Martinez: Liam will author the technical steps, Priya will add Redwood support escalation and the approval template, Rajesh will add switch firmware details and run the canary.
05:23 Olivia Grant: what about circuit breaker thresholds? currently the service fallback kicks in after three consecutive 5xx on a route, can we tune for earlier fallback to reduce tail amplification?
05:33 Priya Rao: we can adjust thresholds per-route; propose 2 failures within 30s to trigger fallback for the pilot routes.
05:40 Rajesh Patel: fine, let's try that on the canary prefix.
05:44 Liam Chen: also worth noting a mitigation: prefix caching can be warmed by seeding common prompts during canary warmup; that reduces cold-KV misses during the test.
05:54 Maya Flores: can you add the seed prompts to the shared sheet?
05:57 Liam Chen: will do. link will be in the runbook.
06:01 Ava Martinez: quick break for questions from security?
06:04 Ethan Cole: one more — audit logs for the RPC calls, do you capture request IDs and route decisions in the logs persisted to our SIEM?
06:12 Priya Rao: yes request_id is included, route decision and model variant are in the debug trace; we'll make sure payload-less metadata is sent to your SIEM connector and not raw text.
06:22 Ethan Cole: perfect, just need configuration example.
06:25 Priya Rao: we'll attach the config snippet.
06:28 Rajesh Patel: anything on capacity? last week we saw queuing at peak, do we need to bump reserved capacity for the canary?
06:36 Liam Chen: no immediate bump — we have burst policies that will add small extra capacity, but if you expect sustained peak we recommend a short dedicated reservation for the test window.
06:47 Olivia Grant: cost estimate for a two-hour canary with a short reservation?
06:50 Ava Martinez: rough ballpark, for your expected token volume it's ~ $120 for two hours of dedicated buffer, plus telemetry extension cost of about $40. we'll send formal numbers.
07:01 Rajesh Patel: ok that's fine. schedule wise — we target canary 2026-05-12 at 10:00 UTC, run windows of 90 minutes, and then roll to 8 nodes on 2026-05-14 if stable.
07:14 Maya Flores: we'll confirm that slot and ensure KMS rotations are clear.
07:18 Ava Martinez: great. final recap: Liam to produce MTU checklist and iperf commands, Priya to extend telemetry and share SIEM config, Rajesh/Maya to run canary and paste results, Ethan to coordinate ICMP temporary approval. Document owners and due dates in the action items.
07:36 (multiple participants agree)
07:40 Ava Martinez: thanks all; we'll follow up with the runbook link and the benchmark-sheet.
07:45 Rajesh Patel: thanks, talk soon.

Attachments/links referenced: benchmark-sheet (internal link), runbook-draft (link), security-questionnaire (link).

End of transcript.
